chunks: And whatever is in it from Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr, I have narrated it from my father and from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan—may Allah be pleased with them both—who said: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī together narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr al-Baṣrī.

key_terms.الْبَصْرِيِّ: al-Baṣrī; a nisbah identifying Yāsīn as being from Baṣrah
key_terms.الْحِمْيَرِيُّ: al-Ḥimyarī; a nisbah identifying one of the transmitters
key_terms.حَدَّثَنَا: narrated to us; a formal transmission term in hadith chains
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicating the author’s narration of the report
key_terms.يَاسِينَ الضَّرِيرِ: Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr, the narrator to whom this transmission chain leads

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage provides the sanad/isnad for reports transmitted from Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh. Its significance lies in documenting the line of transmission through the author’s teachers back to the Basran narrator Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr.
